memory_update.text: Add ServiceNow (NOW), Salesforce (CRM), Snowflake (SNOW), Okta (OKTA), and Datadog (DDOG) as primary Layer 1B public-market candidates for the enterprise agentic software/data/security node.

For this node, the investable chokepoints cluster into four control layers: workflow surfaces, governed enterprise data context, identity/non-human identity governance, and production observability/security.

Workday (WDAY) has strong systems-of-record relevance through HR/finance workflows and an Agent System of Record, but was not included in the top-five candidate list because the pass prioritized broader cross-enterprise workflow, data, identity and observability coverage.

SailPoint (SAIL) and CyberArk exposure should be revisited in a dedicated identity-security pass. SailPoint is newly public again and directly targets agent identity security; CyberArk's standalone public mapping may be affected by Palo Alto Networks acquisition developments and should be verified before inclusion.

Palantir (PLTR), Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOGL) and Amazon (AMZN) remain relevant to enterprise AI platforms and cloud-agent infrastructure but were not repeated here because they are already represented in the seed universe or belong partly to broader cloud/platform layers.

node: Enterprise agentic software, workflow automation, data platforms, identity and AI governance
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the AI software chokepoint suggests the investable universe should extend beyond model providers and generic AI apps into vendors that own enterprise workflow surfaces, governed data context, identity controls, and production observability. The highest-relevance public mappings in this pass are ServiceNow and Salesforce for workflow/CRM agent surfaces, Snowflake for governed enterprise data context, Okta for agent/non-human identity control, and Datadog for AI-agent/LLM observability and security. These are research candidates only, not buy/sell recommendations.
